partner_context.their_ambition: GVB runs public transport for Amsterdam — metro, tram, bus and the free IJ ferries that carry pedestrians and cyclists across the water to Amsterdam-Noord. The municipality has committed that all of the city's ferries will become emission-free, and has begun introducing new electric vessels. Its ambition on the IJ is a fully zero-emission crossing for a network that already moves tens of thousands of people a day at no fare.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the foiling-electric upgrade to a ferry network GVB already runs and is already electrifying. The Central Station–Buiksloterweg crossing and the longer runs to IJplein and NDSM — flown clear of the water: faster, near-silent, low-wake and zero-emission, free at the point of use, from the pontoons that already exist.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Amsterdam, Netherlands · GVB (Amsterdam municipal transport)
hero.title: Navier × Amsterdam Ferries — the IJ, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on GVB's free IJ crossings to Amsterdam-Noord and NDSM: faster, quieter and all-electric public transport across the water GVB is already committed to decarbonising.
hero.what_we_do_together: GVB brings the IJ ferry network, the pontoons and the public-transport mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and the certification path. Together we run the same crossings — faster and zero-emission — extending the electrification the city has already begun.

why_now: Amsterdam has committed that every city ferry becomes emission-free and has begun rolling out electric vessels, inside a city targeting climate neutrality by 2050 and a car-light centre now. The mandate is set and the pontoons are in place; a foiling-electric fleet is how the longer IJ runs to NDSM get faster while going fully clean, with low wake on a busy, cargo-shared waterway.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the GVB network right behind Centraal Station, where the IJ ferries meet the metro, tram and train. A passenger steps off a national train and straight onto a foil to Noord or NDSM — free, fast and clean — while the short high-frequency shuttles keep the heaviest cycle-and-pedestrian loads underneath.

journeys_unlocked.label: Centraal Station ↔ Buiksloterweg
journeys_unlocked.today: The busiest free IJ crossing — a short, high-frequency shuttle to Amsterdam-Noord.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A near-silent, zero-emission crossing that keeps the free service and adds clean, low-wake capacity.

journeys_unlocked.label: Centraal Station ↔ NDSM Werf
journeys_unlocked.today: The longer run west to the NDSM creative district — slow on today's diesel ferries.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A direct foiling link to NDSM: the longer IJ run is exactly where foiling turns slow into fast, and diesel into zero-emission.

journeys_unlocked.label: Centraal Station ↔ IJplein
journeys_unlocked.today: A steady commuter crossing to the IJplein neighbourhood in Noord.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A quiet, clean commuter link on the same free ticket, gentle on a working waterway.

differentiation.why_navier: The platform is purpose-built for this network: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (vital on shared and protected waters), near-silent, zero-emission, and viable year-round. It delivers the authority's published decarbonisation commitment on the links where speed and wake have kept older vessels in service.

proof_points.claim: The city has committed to emission-free ferries.
proof_points.evidence: Amsterdam has stated all city ferries will become emission-free and has introduced new electric IJ ferries.

proof_points.claim: The IJ ferries are public transport, not tourism.
proof_points.evidence: The F1–F7 IJ crossings are free, run as part of GVB's public-transport network, and carry pedestrians and cyclists across the water.
Amsterdam targets climate neutrality and has one of Europe's most aggressive zero-emission zone programmes.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Will it slow down a busy, cargo-shared waterway?
objections.response: No — the platform is low-wake and precise; it shares the IJ courteously with commercial traffic and keeps to the ferry corridors GVB already runs.

objections.concern: The ferries are free — does this change that?
objections.response: No — it stays a free public crossing; Navier changes the propulsion and the speed on the longer runs, not the fare.

objections.concern: Does this replace the ferries people rely on?
objections.response: No — the short high-frequency shuttles keep the heaviest loads; foiling adds a faster, cleaner layer on the longer IJ runs.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path.
the_ask.partner_brings: The ferry route map, the piers/stops, the single-ticket integration, and the published decarbonisation mandate.
the_ask.next_step: Identify the first GVB IJ link — most likely the longer Centraal–NDSM run — for a foiling-electric public pilot on the free crossing.

close.body: Amsterdam has already committed that every city ferry goes emission-free. Navier is how the longer IJ crossings get faster while going fully clean — a quiet, zero-emission ride to Noord and NDSM, free at the point of use, and gentle on a working waterway.
